g.title: G
cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale Agents with more incident edges in a layer have more opportunities for exposure transitions attributed to that layer, so per-layer degree can raise the likelihood of a layer-attributed exposure event.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge upward Higher per-agent contact degree in a layer increases exposure opportunities along recorded edges, raising the layer-level exposure incidence per edge.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_meso_layer_active_run upward Agents with many contacts in a layer can sustain transmission chains across consecutive sampled steps, lengthening the layer's active exposure run.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy upward Heterogeneous per-agent degree across layers concentrates exposure activity in high-degree settings, shifting the cross-layer entropy of attributed exposures.
p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale A larger per-layer weight load can make exposures more likely to be attributed to that same contact layer.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward Higher per-edge exposure incidence in a layer indicates more active transmission there, increasing the chance that a new exposure event is attributed to that layer rather than to another setting.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_micro_layer_beta_load downward Uneven degree distribution within a contact layer can place a subset of agents under much heavier contact-weight load, shaping their per-layer beta load.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Concentration of layer degree among few agents can raise exposure incidence per edge by concentrating contact opportunities.
p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_meso_layer_active_run intra_scale Highly uneven layer degree can sustain repeated attributed exposures in a layer by repeatedly involving high-degree agents.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy upward Within-layer degree dispersion creates core-periphery contact patterns that make some layers dominate exposure production, changing cross-layer incidence entropy.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward A layer that has sustained consecutive active exposure steps creates a locally infectious setting, increasing the chance that an individual's new exposure is attributed to that layer through repeated opportunities for contact within it.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale A layer that has been active for consecutive steps may accumulate susceptible depletion, changing the per-edge incidence rate in that setting.

p2_macro_layer_edge_turnover → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward High edge-set turnover breaks contact continuity within a setting, reducing the chance that any recorded edge repeatedly carries transmission and thereby lowering attributed exposure incidence per edge in that layer.

p2_macro_layer_edge_turnover → p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy intra_scale High edge turnover redistributes contact opportunities across layers, plausibly changing how evenly exposures are spread across settings.

p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward When exposures are more evenly distributed across layers (higher entropy), the probability that a given new exposure is attributed to any particular layer falls, because no layer dominates the exposure mix.

p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy → p2_meso_layer_active_run downward Higher entropy means exposure activity is spread across more contact layers; this dilution reduces the likelihood that any single layer sustains consecutive active exposure steps, shortening its active run.

N8 | p2_micro_layer_degree Agent contact degree within a contact layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: d_i,l(t) = number of distinct contact records at step t in layer l with agent_id = i plus those with partner_id = i, de-duplicated by unordered pair so that a reciprocal pair counts once; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N9 | p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag Agent exposure transition attributed to a layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: E_i,l(t) = 1 if X_i(t) = 1 and the layer recorded on the exposure event for that agent and step equals l; 0 if X_i(t) = 1 and the recorded layer is non-null and different from l; undefined if X_i(t) = 0, if the recorded layer is null, or if no exposure event can be matched. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N10 | p2_micro_layer_beta_load Agent per-layer contact weight load Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: W_i,l(t) = sum of beta over the undirected contact edges at step t in layer l incident to agent i; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N11 | p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge Layer exposure incidence per contact edge Scale: meso | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: lambda_l(t) = (sum over agents i of E_i,l(t)) / N_l(t), where N_l(t) is the number of distinct undirected edges recorded in layer l at step t; undefined when N_l(t) = 0. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N12 | p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion Within-layer degree dispersion Scale: meso | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: CV_l(t) = SD_i(d_i,l(t)) / mean_i(d_i,l(t)) over agents observed at step t in layer l; undefined when fewer than two agents have defined degree or when the mean is 0. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N13 | p2_meso_layer_active_run Layer consecutive active-step run length Scale: meso | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: L_l(t) = k where k is the largest integer such that for every observed step s in the k consecutive observed steps ending at t, sum over i of E_i,l(s) > 0; L_l(t) = 0 if the layer has no attributed exposure at t; undefined if step t is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N14 | p2_macro_layer_edge_turnover Layer edge-set Jaccard turnover Scale: macro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: J_l(t) = 1 - |A_l(t) intersect A_l(t-1)| / |A_l(t) union A_l(t-1)|, where A_l(t) is the set of unordered agent pairs recorded as edges in layer l at step t; undefined when the union is empty or t-1 is not observed. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N15 | p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy Normalised entropy of layer exposure shares Scale: macro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: H(t) = -(sum over layers l of p_l(t) * ln p_l(t)) / ln(n(t)), where p_l(t) is the share of layer-attributed exposure transitions at t falling in layer l and n(t) is the number of layers with non-zero share; undefined when n(t) < 2.
